Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. FY26 repurchases of HK$283.5m (RMB260.0m) funded more than the flat count.

inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1724 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16 22:02Z). Statements are RMB (filing: 'Expressed in RMB'); the HKEX quote is HKD. No dual listing to parity-check; sanity: FY26 repurchases HK$283.53m = RMB259.87m implies 1.091 HKD/RMB over Sep-25..Mar-26 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X ran 1.146-1.173 Apr-Oct 2026, RMB appreciating), confirming the direction (HKD per RMB > 1). All flows and the equity bridge are RMB; per-share values convert to HKD at this rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are RMB, so the rate is RMB-built: China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta ~1.25 x ERP ~6.5% + ~0.6% small-cap/VIE-governance premium = ~10.5% cost of equity. Company is net cash (debt is bills-discounted borrowings), so WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in every scenario: risk lives in the scenario flows and weights, charged once.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): lease liabilities (RMB6.1m) included in total_debt; no lease charge in the flows. Lease cash is immaterial (FY26 principal+interest RMB2.0m).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%); NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at book RMB58.4m. NCI share of FY26 profit was RMB6.1m.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US') + adaptations. Yidu is an operating healthcare data/AI software and services company (AI for Medical big-data platforms for hospitals/governments, Life Sciences RWE/clinical solutions for pharma, Care/Hui Min Bao health insurance management). It is not distressed, not a cash shell and not under a corporate action, so a going-concern FCF model applies. But FY2026 is its FIRST profitable year and the reported RMB78.8m profit is entirely treasury income: operating profit RMB87.8m includes RMB145.4m interest on term deposits / fixed-rate notes (other income note 6) and RMB19.1m other gains (fair-value gains on WMP/swaps). Stripping those, core operating loss is ~RMB-76.6m, core EBITDA after SBC ~RMB-39.9m and pre-SBC core EBITDA ~RMB-14m (-1.7% of revenue), vs ~-35% in FY2025 (admin staff cost cut RMB100m->25m, impairments RMB79m->29m). Hence driver year 1 starts near breakeven, not at the headline profit. Value is therefore dominated by the RMB3.35bn net financial-asset position; the operating business is modelled from components. INTEREST: only RMB1.76m of interest sits in OCF ('interest received'); the RMB97.4m of term-deposit interest is received in INVESTING, so it is already outside reported FCF; last_fcf strips only the 1.76m. The treasury assets carry the stripped income in the bridge. NET CASH (31-Mar-2026, RMB m): cash 664.8 + term deposits 1,392.6 + fixed-rate notes at amortised cost (Goldman/JPM/Citi, mature 2027-30) 1,204.0 + accrued interest 53.5 + FVTPL (WMP, total-return swap, VC fund) 103.3 = 3,418.2, less borrowings 65.0 and leases 6.1. Pledged/restricted deposits (22.4) excluded. Remaining unfunded commitment to YD Capital I fund ~US$26.8m is a cash-to-investment swap at fair value and is not deducted. Market cap at the quote (RMB~2.46bn on 1,004.5m outstanding) is ~0.73x net financial assets: the market is pricing either continued burn, cash misallocation, or a governance/VIE discount on the cash. BUYBACKS: RMB260.0m in FY26 - the flat count is funded.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (losses and buybacks shrink book) and EPS/owner-FCF are negative at the start points, so CAGRs on them are undefined. Revenue is flat over 5 years (FY21 867 -> FY26 819) with a FY22 spike to 1,237 and a reset in FY23. Selected rate is the 3yr revenue CAGR; forward base growth (10% decelerating) leans on FY26's +14.6% and is a judgment, not the historical rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - OCF interest), RMB m: FY21 ~-481, FY22 ~-866, FY23 ~-485, FY24 ~-432, FY25 ~-360, FY26 -79.3. Negative throughout, improving sharply; H2 FY26 OCF turned positive (+RMB29.3m). SBC has fallen from 14% of revenue (FY22) to 3.2%.

base.narrative: FY26 operating-leverage gains hold; revenue grows ~10% on Life Sciences RWE and Care/Hui Min Bao, with Medical big-data flat-to-up; pre-SBC EBITDA margin climbs from ~breakeven to 15% by year 8.

scenario_narratives.base: Yidu holds the FY26 cost reset (admin and R&D cut ~RMB100m) and grows ~10% a year as pharma real-world-evidence and clinical-trial work (17 of the top 20 MNCs as clients) and the Hui Min Bao city-insurance/Care business compound, while the hospital/government big-data segment, budget-constrained by local-government finances, grows slowly. Receivable impairments normalise. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin reaches 15% (owner-FCF ~9-10%) by year 8. The RMB3.35bn treasury is preserved and not wasted.
scenario_narratives.bull: YiduCore/medical large-model deployment converts into recurring platform revenue across hospitals, pharma and insurers; China's push on medical AI and data-element policy accelerates hospital procurement; Life Sciences wins more global RWE mandates. Revenue compounds mid-teens for five years and the software-like mix lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 22%.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY26's breakeven was a one-off cost cut, not operating leverage: local-government and hospital IT budgets stay squeezed, AI commoditises the data-platform offer (large-model vendors and hospital in-house builds), pharma RWE spend in China stays soft, and receivables keep being impaired. Revenue grows ~2-3%, EBITDA hovers near zero and the business burns cash for most of the decade; terminal value close to nil. Value collapses to the net cash less the burn.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (up from the 15% default): FY26 is the first profitable year and the operating business was still loss-making ex treasury income; customers are budget-constrained Chinese hospitals and local governments, and receivable impairments are recurrent. Base 50%: the cost reset is real and H2 FY26 OCF was positive. Bull 20% (down from 35%): it needs both AI-platform monetisation and a hospital-budget recovery to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Yidu's value is mostly its balance sheet: ~RMB3.3/share of net financial assets (term deposits, IG bank notes, cash) against a quote that converts to ~RMB2.45/share. The operating business is valued on owner FCF built from a near-breakeven core (FY26 profit was treasury interest, not operations). Even the bear case, where the operation is worth little, leaves value near net cash less the burn; the question is whether management and the controlling holder let shareholders keep the cash.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash access / governance: offshore-listed VIE structure; the market already prices the treasury at ~0.73x. Buybacks (RMB260m in FY26) are the strongest counter-evidence.
FY26 operating breakeven may reflect a one-off staff-cost cut and lower impairments rather than durable leverage.
Customer budget risk: hospitals, local governments and Hui Min Bao programmes depend on public finances.
Receivables (RMB378m + RMB65m contract assets on RMB819m revenue) and their impairment.
Price has fallen ~53% since March 2026 with no H1 FY27 filing yet extracted; the interim (due ~Nov 2026) could reset cash or margins.
Unfunded VC fund commitment (~US$26.8m) and strategic investments may divert cash.
